content: Teaching in medical education is defined as a formal and organized process of transmitting knowledge to an individual or a group. Methods of Faculty Physicians Faculty physicians employ various methods of teaching, including role modeling and specific teaching tactics. While some aspects of these methods overlap, others may conflict. Being knowledgeable and efficient are essential attributes for role modeling, and these qualities also serve as important teaching tactics. However, many attributes required for effective role modeling may take time to develop, which can conflict with the need for efficiency in teaching tactics. Teaching Tactics Teaching tactics utilized by individual faculty members during clinical care have been validated and include the following: Creating a conducive learning climate Session control: This involves maintaining efficiency, adhering to time constraints, setting a clear agenda, and avoiding unnecessary digressions. Communication of goals: Clearly articulating the objectives of the teaching session. Promoting understanding and retention: Ensuring that learners grasp and retain the material being taught. Evaluation: Assessing the learner’s progress and understanding. Providing feedback: Offering constructive and actionable feedback to learners. Encouraging self-directed learning: Guiding learners to take initiative in their own education. Teacher’s knowledge: Demonstrating expertise and directing learners to utilize relevant literature, while also discussing perspectives beyond the teacher’s own viewpoint. Role Modeling The behavior of high-quality physician role models encompasses several attributes that have been recommended or studied: Curiosity: Demonstrating a genuine interest in learning and discovery. Caring, humanism, and kindness: Exhibiting compassion and empathy in interactions. Competence in clinical skills: Displaying proficiency and a strong knowledge base in clinical practice. Critical thinking: Applying analytical and evaluative skills in clinical decision-making. Humility: Acknowledging limitations and being open to learning from others. Promotion of self-directed learning: Encouraging learners to take responsibility for their own educational growth. It is important to note that learners’ perspectives on the attributes of effective role models may differ from the attributes that faculty members themselves value.
